objective_pt: Falar de um desentendimento com diplomacia: expressar incômodo sem acusar, reconhecer o outro lado e propor uma solução.

teacher.goal_pt: Conversar sobre conflitos comuns no trabalho e perceber se o aluno usa "discuss" no sentido de brigar.
prompts: What usually causes problems between colleagues?
How do you deal with a difficult coworker?
watchFor: Dizer "we discussed" querendo dizer "brigamos"; "discutir" nesse sentido é "argue".
Dizer "I was very chateated"; "chateado" é "upset" ou "annoyed".

exercises.prompt: I see where you're coming from, but I see it differently.
accepted: I see where you're coming from, but I see it differently.
I see where you are coming from, but I see it differently.

exercises.instruction_pt: "Eles discutiram feio na reunião." Which verb fits best?
exercises.explanation_pt: "Argue" é discutir no sentido de brigar. "Discuss" é conversar sobre um assunto, sem briga.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eu fiquei chateado com o comentário dele."
accepted: I was upset by his comment
I was upset about his comment
I got upset about his comment
I was annoyed by his comment
I was annoyed at his comment
I was annoyed about his comment
I was bothered by his comment
His comment upset me
His comment annoyed me
His comment bothered me
I felt upset about his comment

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Ficamos chateados "with" uma pessoa, mas "about" ou "by" uma coisa: "upset about his comment".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was upset about his comment.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Fiquei chateado" não é "I stayed" (permaneci). Use "I was" ou "I got upset".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was upset about his comment.

teacher.goal_pt: Aprender vocabulário para conflitos: clash, misunderstanding, take it personally, sort out, common ground.
prompts: Have you ever had a misunderstanding with a colleague?
How did you sort it out?
watchFor: Dizer "I take it personal"; o correto é "personally".

exercises.example_en: I think it was just a misunderstanding.
Let's sit down and sort this out.
Please don't take it personally, it's just feedback.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each expression to its meaning.

pairs.pt: bater de frente, entrar em conflito
se meter no espaço de alguém

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Não leve para o lado pessoal."
accepted: Don't take it personally
Please don't take it personally
Try not to take it personally
Do not take it personally
It's nothing personal
Don't take this personally

commonErrors.explanation_pt: O advérbio é "personally": "Don't take it personally". "Personal side" é tradução literal.
O imperativo negativo usa "don't": "Don't take it personally".

teacher.goal_pt: Treinar um tom calmo e a tônica de palavras longas (misunderSTANDing, apoLOgize).
prompts: How does your voice sound when you are calm?
watchFor: Falar rápido e alto demais, o que soa agressivo em inglês.

exercises.prompt: I think there's been a misunderstanding.
accepted: I think there's been a misunderstanding.
I think there has been a misunderstanding.
I think there was a misunderstanding.

exercises.prompt: I apologize if I came across as rude.
accepted: I apologize if I came across as rude.
I apologise if I came across as rude.
I'm sorry if I came across as rude.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Apologize" não é reflexivo: "I apologize", sem "me" (diferente de "eu me desculpo").
commonErrors.correction_en: I apologize if I came across as rude.

exercises.instruction_pt: Where is the main stress in "misunderstanding"?
exercises.explanation_pt: A sílaba mais forte é "STAND". Tônica errada em palavras longas atrapalha mais a compreensão do que um som errado.

teacher.goal_pt: Entender reclamações indiretas de colegas e responder sem ficar na defensiva.
prompts: How would you answer if a colleague said you were always late?
How do you show you're listening?
watchFor: Responder com "It's not my fault" imediatamente; treinar reconhecer antes.
Usar "You always..." e "You never...", que soam como acusação.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What is the colleague's real problem?
exercises.listen: I don't mind helping out, but I've ended up doing your part of the report three times this month.
options: She is doing too much of the other person's work.
She doesn't want to help at all.
exercises.explanation_pt: "I don't mind helping out, but..." suaviza a reclamação. O problema é ter feito a parte do outro três vezes.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. Acknowledge the problem and apologize.
exercises.listen: Honestly, it's frustrating when you change the plan without telling me.
accepted: You're right, I'm sorry. I should have told you
You're right. I should have told you
I'm sorry, I should have told you
Sorry, I should have let you know
I'm sorry, I should've told you
I understand. I'm sorry I didn't tell you
I see your point. I'm sorry I didn't tell you
That's fair. I'm sorry I didn't let you know
I'm sorry about that. It won't happen again
You're right, I'm sorry. It won't happen again
I apologize. I should have told you
I'm sorry, I didn't realize. I'll keep you in the loop

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Para falar de algo que não fizemos no passado: "should have told" (na fala, "should've told").
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm sorry, I should have told you.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Você tem razão" é "You're right". "You have reason" é tradução literal.
commonErrors.correction_en: You're right, I'm sorry. I should have told you.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. Suggest talking about it calmly in private.
exercises.listen: I can't believe you said that in front of the whole team!
accepted: Can we talk about this in private?
Can we talk about it in private?
Could we discuss this in private?
Let's talk about this in private
Let's talk about it in private
Why don't we talk about this in private?
Can we talk about this somewhere private?
Can we talk about this one on one?
I'm sorry. Can we talk about this privately?
Let's sit down and talk about it privately
Can we discuss this later, just the two of us?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Em particular" (a sós) é "in private" ou "privately". "In particular" significa "especificamente".
commonErrors.correction_en: Can we talk about this in private?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Discuss" não leva "about": "discuss this". Ou use "talk about this".
commonErrors.correction_en: Could we discuss this in private?

teacher.goal_pt: Resolver um conflito em uma simulação: falar do impacto ("I feel..."), ouvir e propor uma solução.
prompts: You keep missing my deadlines. What's going on?
How do you think we could fix this?
Can we agree on something for next time?
watchFor: Começar com "You always..."; incentivar "I've noticed that..." e "I feel...".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eu percebi que a gente tem tido alguns problemas de comunicação."
accepted: I've noticed that we've been having some communication problems
I've noticed that we've had some communication problems
I've noticed we've been having some communication problems
I've noticed that we've been having some communication issues
I've noticed that we've been having some problems with communication
I noticed that we've been having some communication problems
I noticed we've had some communication issues
I've realized that we've been having some communication problems

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Perceber" no sentido de notar é "notice" ou "realize". "Perceive" é formal e mais ligado a interpretação.
commonErrors.correction_en: I've noticed that we've been having some communication problems.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Tem tido" fala de algo que começou antes e continua: use o present perfect, "we've been having" ou "we've had".
commonErrors.correction_en: We've been having some communication problems.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eu pretendo falar com ela amanhã para resolver isso."
accepted: I intend to talk to her tomorrow to sort this out
I'm planning to talk to her tomorrow to sort this out
I plan to talk to her tomorrow to sort this out
I'm going to talk to her tomorrow to sort this out
I'm going to speak to her tomorrow to sort it out
I plan to talk to her tomorrow to solve this
I'm planning to talk to her tomorrow to resolve this
I intend to speak with her tomorrow to sort this out
I'm going to talk to her tomorrow to fix this

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Pretend" é falso cognato: significa fingir. "Pretender" é "intend", "plan" ou "be going to".
commonErrors.correction_en: I intend to talk to her tomorrow to sort this out.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Para indicar finalidade usamos "to", e não "for": "to sort this out".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm going to talk to her tomorrow to sort this out.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to find common ground.
accepted: I think we both want the same thing here

exercises.instruction_pt: Your colleague keeps sending work late, and it affects you. Talk to them diplomatically.
exercises.prompt_en: Hey, you wanted to talk to me? Is something wrong?
guidelines_pt: Describe the situation without blaming: "I've noticed that..."
Say how it affects you: "It puts me in a difficult position because..."
Propose a solution: "What if we...?" or "Could we agree to...?"

teacher.goal_pt: Revisar a linguagem diplomática e os falsos cognatos "discuss" e "pretend".
prompts: How do you say you disagree without sounding rude?
What's the difference between argue and discuss?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eles brigaram por causa do projeto."
accepted: They argued about the project
They had an argument about the project
They had a fight about the project
They fought over the project
They argued over the project
They had a disagreement about the project
They clashed over the project
They got into an argument about the project

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Discuss" é conversar sobre algo. Para briga, use "argue" ou "have an argument".
"Brigar por causa de" algo soa melhor com "about" ou "over": "argue about the project".

exercises.sentence: Let's sit down and sort this ___.
accepted: out

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "sort out" (resolver): "sort this out".
commonErrors.correction_en: Let's sit down and sort this out.

exercises.instruction_pt: Which sentence sounds the least aggressive?
options: I feel a bit frustrated when the plan changes at the last minute.
You always change the plan at the last minute.
exercises.explanation_pt: Falar do próprio sentimento ("I feel...") e evitar "always" e "never" deixa a conversa mais aberta.

exercises.prompt: I'm glad we talked. Let's keep each other in the loop.
accepted: I'm glad we talked. Let's keep each other in the loop.
I am glad we talked. Let us keep each other in the loop.
